rows.question: What is the difference between the RAG-Sequence and RAG-Token models?
rows.answer: The RAG-Sequence model approximates the seq2seq probability p(y|x) using a top-K approximation, while the RAG-Token model can draw a different latent document for each target token and marginalize accordingly. [rag_lewis2020.pdf, p.3]

rows.question: How did the RAG paper demonstrate updating the model's knowledge by swapping the index?
rows.answer: The RAG paper demonstrated updating the model's knowledge by swapping the index through experiments where they used different indices for the same set of questions. They found that accuracy was higher when using the index that matched the year of the world leaders being queried. For instance, using the 2016 index for 2016 world leaders resulted in 70% accuracy, while using the 2018 index for 2018 world leaders resulted in 68% accuracy. However, accuracy dropped significantly to 12% and 4% when mismatched indices were used, indicating that the model's performance is sensitive to the index used. [rag_lewis2020.pdf, p.8]

rows.question: What training trick does DPR use to reuse other questions' passages as negatives?
rows.answer: DPR uses distantly-supervised passages, specifically BM25 passages, as negatives for other questions in the same batch. [dpr_karpukhin2020.pdf, p.6]

rows.question: What are reflection tokens in Self-RAG?
rows.answer: Reflection tokens in Self-RAG are special tokens that indicate the need for retrieval and the quality of generation. They are categorized into retrieval tokens and critique tokens. [selfrag_asai2023.pdf, p.1]

rows.question: How is the training data for the Self-RAG critic model created?
rows.answer: The training data for the Self-RAG critic model is created by running the critic model to assess if additional passages could enhance generation, adding the retrieval special token if retrieval is needed, and then evaluating the relevance of each passage and predicting ISREL for relevant passages, as described in [selfrag_asai2023.pdf, p.5].
